verses.text: Now when men began to multiply on the face of the earth and daughters were born to them,
the sons of God saw that the daughters of men were beautiful, and they took as wives whomever they chose.
So the LORD said, "My Spirit will not contend with man forever, for he is mortal; his days shall be 120 years."

The Nephilim were on the earth in those days—and afterward as well—when the sons of God had relations with the daughters of men. And they bore them children who became the mighty men of old, men of renown.
Then the LORD saw that the wickedness of man was great upon the earth, and that every inclination of the thoughts of his heart was altogether evil all the time.
And the LORD regretted that He had made man on the earth, and He was grieved in His heart.
So the LORD said, "I will blot out man, whom I have created, from the face of the earth—every man and beast and crawling creature and bird of the air—for I am grieved that I have made them."
Noah, however, found favor in the eyes of the LORD.
This is the account of Noah. Noah was a righteous man, blameless in his generation; Noah walked with God.
And Noah had three sons: Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
Now the earth was corrupt in the sight of God, and full of violence.
And God looked upon the earth and saw that it was corrupt; for all living creatures on the earth had corrupted their ways.
Then God said to Noah, "The end of all living creatures has come before Me, because through them the earth is full of violence. Now behold, I will destroy both them and the earth.
Make for yourself an ark of gopher wood; make rooms in the ark and coat it with pitch inside and out.
And this is how you are to build it: The ark is to be 300 cubits long, 50 cubits wide, and 30 cubits high.
You are to make a roof for the ark, finish its walls a cubit from the top, place a door in the side of the ark, and build lower, middle, and upper decks.
And behold, I will bring floodwaters upon the earth to destroy every creature under the heavens that has the breath of life. Everything on the earth will perish.
But I will establish My covenant with you, and you will enter the ark—you and your sons and your wife and your sons' wives with you.
And you are to bring two of every living creature into the ark—male and female—to keep them alive with you.
Two of every kind of bird and animal and crawling creature will come to you to be kept alive.
You are also to take for yourself every kind of food that is eaten and gather it as food for yourselves and for the animals."
So Noah did everything precisely as God had commanded him.

context.author: Genesis names no author. Jewish and Christian tradition, and the New Testament’s way of speaking of “the Law of Moses” (Luke 24:44), credit the five books of the Law to Moses. Many scholars think Genesis was gathered and shaped from older sources over a long time, and a few remarks look back from a later day: “at that time the Canaanites were in the land” (Genesis 12:6).
context.genre: Narrative of beginnings (Genesis 1-11): creation, the first family, the flood and the nations, with genealogies
context.audience: Israel, God’s covenant people, learning who their God is, where the world came from and what went wrong with it
context.mapLabel: MESOPOTAMIA, THE LAND OF THE FLOOD STORIES
context.setting: As people multiply, “the sons of God” take wives from “the daughters of men,” and the Nephilim are on the earth (vv.1-4). “The LORD saw that the wickedness of man was great upon the earth, and that every inclination of the thoughts of his heart was altogether evil all the time” (v.5). He regrets that He made man and is grieved in His heart (v.6). “Noah, however, found favor in the eyes of the LORD” (v.8): a righteous man, blameless in his generation, who walked with God (v.9). God tells Noah that He will bring a flood, and orders him to build an ark of gopher wood, 300 cubits long, 50 wide and 30 high, with rooms, pitch inside and out, a roof and three decks (vv.13-16). God will make His covenant with Noah, and his family and two of every kind of animal will go in with him (vv.18-21). “So Noah did everything precisely as God had commanded him” (v.22).
context.custom: A cubit was the length from elbow to fingertip, about 18 inches (45 cm), so the ark was roughly 450 by 75 by 45 feet (137 x 23 x 14 m), a long box built to float, not to sail. The same word for the ark, tevah, is used only once more in the Bible: for the basket of reeds, coated with pitch, in which baby Moses was laid on the Nile (Exodus 2:3). “Gopher wood” is not known; cypress is a common guess.
context.timelineImmediate: Chapter 7 tells how Noah, his family and the animals entered the ark, and the flood covered the earth.
context.timelineBible: Who “the sons of God” were is debated: angels (as in 1 Enoch, and perhaps Jude 1:6 and 2 Peter 2:4), the line of Seth, or ancient kings. Jesus said, “As it was in the days of Noah, so will it be at the coming of the Son of Man” (Matthew 24:37). Hebrews says Noah, “warned about things not yet seen, in godly fear built an ark to save his family” (Hebrews 11:7), and Peter calls him a preacher of righteousness (2 Peter 2:5).

translation.meaning: To be sorry, to grieve, to relent; the same word that gave Noah his name (5:29). The LORD is grieved over the people He made.
Grace, favor: what one is given, not earned. Noah means ‘rest’; chen spells his name backwards in Hebrew.
A box or chest; only here and for Moses’ basket on the Nile (Exodus 2:3). A different word is used for the ark of the covenant.
A covenant: a binding agreement sealed by oath. This is the first time the word appears in the Bible.

gospelParallels.note: As it was in the days of Noah, so will the coming of the Son of Man be.
By faith Noah built an ark to save his family.
God did not spare the ancient world, but protected Noah.

overview.summary: The earth is filled with violence and every thought of man’s heart is evil, so God, grieved, resolves to send a flood; but Noah finds favor and is told to build an ark, and he does all that God commands.
overview.placeName: Babel in the land of Shinar (Babylon)

history.t: Mesopotamia told of a great flood and a man who built a boat.
Giants of old, the men of renown.

archaeology.t: A Babylonian epic (about 1700 BC) in which the gods send a flood and one man survives in a boat.
Natural tar was used in Mesopotamia to waterproof boats and buildings.

overview.discussion: “Noah did everything precisely as God had commanded him” (v.22), long before any rain fell. What has God asked of me that I am waiting to see proved before I obey?
overview.book: The book of Genesis · 50 chapters. Beginnings: creation, the fall, the flood and the nations, then God’s promise to Abraham, Isaac, Jacob and Joseph.
overview.author: Moses, by tradition

currentImage.caption: The ‘Flood Tablet,’ Tablet 11 of the Epic of Gilgamesh, from the library of the Assyrian king Ashurbanipal at Nineveh (7th century BC, British Museum). Its hero Utnapishtim builds a boat, survives a great flood, and sends out birds to find dry land. The story is older than this copy; how it relates to Genesis is debated.
